topline.lens: Mature public studio site (SIL 960/1000). S186-S190 built and measured a full proof+conversion apparatus; the funnel is data-starved (1 event / 30d, honest-dark) — that is a traffic problem, not a code problem, so this audit does NOT add more measurement. Instead it (a) closes real integration/freshness gaps the proof apparatus left open, (b) extends the machine-SEO spine to the citation layer, and (c) pays down a concrete WCAG gap. Theme: COMPLETE THE PROOF SURFACE + HARDEN ITS HONESTY.
topline.competitiveFrame: The studio's proof manifest (status-proof.json, trustScore 80) has two honest-dark/seed feeds dragging it below 100 and is MISSING the conversion funnel it built. Its agents.json carries prose citation guidance but no structured, dated, machine-readable citation feed — the single thing an LLM most needs to answer 'what is VaultSpark Studios' without hallucinating. And S190's animated session count-up ships with no reduced-motion guard while 40 sibling assets honor it. These are completeness + honesty gaps in infrastructure that already exists, not net-new surfaces.
groundTruthVerified: api/status-proof.json: trustScore=80, feeds=10 — funnel-summary NOT among PROOF_FEEDS (build-status-proof.mjs:33-41). Confirmed integration gap.
api/public-status.json: hardcoded seed, generatedAt 2026-05-22, staleAfterH 720 — crosses the 30d threshold on 2026-06-21, after which it turns the trust manifest amber. Latent landmine.

api/funnel-summary.json: asOf 2026-06-05, totalEvents 1 — deterministic (mirrors latest history day), frozen until traffic arrives. Correct honest-dark behavior; must be treated as expected-not-stale when folded into the manifest.
assets/ignis-answer-engine.js:31 emits to '/v/rum' correctly (grep rendered it as '\v\rum' — a tooling escaping artifact, NOT a bug; verified by Read).
api/citation.json: ABSENT. agents.json:42 has prose citation guidance pointing at llms-full.txt shards but no structured citation data.
assets/honest-traction-scoreboard.js:54-65 + assets/vault-rank-bar.js: requestAnimationFrame count-up with 0 prefers-reduced-motion guards; 40 assets sitewide DO guard. Confirmed WCAG 2.3.3 gap.
session-counter.js named in S190 records does NOT exist as a file — the count-up shipped inside honest-traction-scoreboard.js (commit 8bcb830b). Records mislabel; reconcile at closeout.
S190 features confirmed live on pages.dev origin (status-proof/funnel-summary/public-intelligence all 200, generatedAt today).

items.title: Honor prefers-reduced-motion on the session count-up + rank bars
items.why: S190's animated session count-up (honest-traction-scoreboard.js) and vault-rank-bar.js run requestAnimationFrame animations with no reduced-motion guard — motion-sensitive visitors get an unwanted count-up animation that WCAG 2.3.3 says should be suppressible. 40 other assets already honor the media query, so this is a coverage gap, not a new pattern. Outcome: keyboard- and motion-sensitive visitors reach the membership decision without a vestibular trigger.
items.recipe: In honest-traction-scoreboard.js, before the rAF loop: if window.matchMedia && matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches, set el.textContent = String(target) and return (skip animation). Same guard in vault-rank-bar.js before its bar-fill animation. Grep the two files for requestAnimationFrame and gate each.

items.title: Structured /api/citation.json for accurate LLM citation
items.why: When an LLM is asked 'what is VaultSpark Studios / is it trustworthy', it has agents.json prose guidance but no structured, dated, machine-readable source with the actual citable facts. A canonical citation feed (studio identity, one-line description, 3 CONFIRMED proof metrics pulled from status-proof.json/field-win.json, canonical URL, license, asOf date) gives crawlers an authoritative source so they cite accurately instead of hallucinating. This is the natural next layer of the machine-SEO spine the studio already over-indexes on. Outcome: AI agents answer about VaultSpark with sourced, dated, honest facts (info-finding).
items.recipe: New scripts/build-citation.mjs reads ecosystem-state.json + api/status-proof.json + api/field-win.json (confirmed wins only, honest-dark when none) and writes api/citation.json {schemaVersion, asOf, studio:{name,url,description,license}, claims:[{text, source, asOf}], suggestedCitation:'...'}. Add to agents.json discovery block + a 'Citation' line in llms.txt. Self-test the builder + wire into build + build:check (drift gate). Public-safe: only already-public confirmed metrics.

items.title: Stop the trust manifest from silently rotting on a hardcoded seed
items.why: api/public-status.json is a hardcoded seed ('seed until Hub Worker /public-status endpoint is wired') stamped 2026-05-22 with a 720h (30d) staleAfter — it crosses that threshold on 2026-06-21, after which it quietly drags trustScore down and worstStale reports a month-old feed. The trust manifest's whole job is honesty; a seed that rots into a false 'stale' signal undermines it. Outcome: the public trust score stays honest and an agent reading status-proof.json never sees a phantom-stale feed.
items.recipe: (a) In check-public-contract-health.mjs (the writer), derive public-status.json's mutable signals from real local sources (reposOnline from PROJECT_REGISTRY count, lastArkBroadcastAt/ignisHeartbeatAt from existing feeds) and stamp generatedAt = today on each regen so it tracks reality instead of freezing. (b) Add a check in check-public-contract-health.mjs --self-test (or a small new gate) that ERRORs when any status-proof FEED's committed generatedAt is older than 0.5x its staleAfterH — surfacing seed-rot before it hits prod. Wire into build:check.

items.title: Fold the conversion funnel into the one-fetch proof manifest
items.why: status-proof.json is the studio's self-grading 'one fetch verifies our posture' manifest, but the conversion funnel (funnel-summary.json, built S189) isn't one of its 10 feeds. An agent or visitor reading the canonical proof surface can see uptime, field-wins, and AI-spine health but not the conversion posture. Folding it in completes the proof surface. Critically: funnel-summary is deterministic and frozen until traffic arrives, so it must be marked honest-dark-aware (expected, not stale) or it would drag trustScore. Outcome: the single canonical proof fetch now answers 'how is conversion doing' honestly (info-finding).
items.recipe: Add { key: 'funnel-summary', staleAfterH: null, honestDarkOk: true } to FEEDS in build-status-proof.mjs; in the freshness grader, treat honestDark=true (or staleAfterH=null) feeds as present+fresh (never counted as stale, never the worstStale). Add a self-test case proving a frozen honest-dark funnel keeps trustScore at 100 when all other feeds are fresh. /status/ proof tile already fetches the manifest — confirm it surfaces the new feed.

items.title: Make Oracle answer feedback attributable per query-cluster
items.why: The oracle-answer:{helpful,unhelpful} beacon is global — rollup-rum-ux writes oracle-feedback.ndjson with clusterKey:'*', and the cluster ranker ignores '*' keys, so the helpfulScore signal can never become topic-specific. Carrying the matched cluster id on the vote makes answer quality attributable per topic, which is what build-oracle-query-clusters.mjs's recency-weighted ranker was designed to consume. Honest caveat: the funnel is data-starved, so this builds capability ahead of volume — low immediate ROI but it completes a loop already 80% built. Outcome: when traffic arrives, the studio learns WHICH topics the Oracle answers badly (info-finding).
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js, when an answer renders, stash the matched cluster id (findCluster result) on the feedback control; on vote, emit oracle-answer:helpful:<clusterId> / :unhelpful:<clusterId> (dynamic-prefix allowlist the family in the Worker RUM_UX_EVENTS + check-rum-allowlist). In rollup-rum-ux.mjs updateOracleFeedback, parse the cluster suffix into clusterKey instead of hardcoding '*'. Keep '*' as the fallback when no cluster matched. Update self-tests on both ends.
executionLog: S191: DEFERRED with evidence. Architectural blocker found: cloudflare/security-headers-worker.js RUM_UX_EVENTS is an EXACT-match Set (validateUxEvent → RUM_UX_EVENTS.has(value)), not a prefix-matcher. Cluster keys (oracle-insights.json: 'what_the', etc.) are unbounded/dynamic, so emitting oracle-answer:helpful:<clusterKey> would be silently dropped at the edge — the exact S186 silent-drop class the S188 allowlist gate exists to prevent. Shipping correctly requires a BOUNDED Worker prefix-rule for the oracle-answer: family (charset + length capped) + worker.unit.spec.js coverage + deriveSummary prefix-sum + check-funnel-contract tolerance — a security-surface change across 5 files. Deferred because the funnel is data-starved (1 event / 30d): this builds capability ahead of any volume, and the risk of subtly breaking the funnel aggregation (in build:check) outweighs near-zero current value. rollup-rum-ux updateOracleFeedback already parses r.clusterKey, so the data-layer side is ready; only the Worker acceptance + frontend emit remain. Next session: add the bounded prefix rule to the Worker first, prove it with a unit test, THEN wire the frontend emit + funnel prefix-sum in one change.
